subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper marks an article at such a price that after giving a discount of 12(1)/(2)% on the marked price, he still earns a profit of 15%. If the cost price of the article is Rs. 385, then the sum of the marked price and the selling price (in Rs.) of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 12.5) : (100 + 15) = 87.5 : 115 = 7 : 9.2 = 35 : 46

Given 35 units = ₹385 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹11

MP = 46 × 11 = ₹506 | SP = 385 × 1.15 = ₹442.75

Sum = MP + SP = 506 + 442.75 = ₹948.75

**∴ The correct answer is ₹948.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹385

Profit% = 15%

Discount% = 12.5% = 1/8

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd9efb22ca88d27a83da3f89e8c1056c51f022dac4b7ab7de3335dfa8d3cd996.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

⇒ SP = 385 × (115/100) = 385 × 1.15

⇒ SP = ₹442.75

⇒ Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%)/100 = SP

⇒ MP × (87.5/100) = 442.75

⇒ MP = (442.75 × 100) ÷ 87.5

⇒ MP = 44275 ÷ 87.5 = ₹506

⇒ Sum = MP + SP

⇒ Sum = 506 + 442.75 = ₹948.75

**∴ The correct answer is ₹948.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price displayed on the label. MP = SP + Discount = CP + Markup.

Effective Discount

Successive discounts of a% and b% result in a single discount of [a + b − (a×b)/100]%.
